name: Charles Cornwallis
contribution: As Governor-General of Bengal, Charles Cornwallis oversaw the 1793 Permanent Settlement, which fixed the Company's land revenue demand and recognized zamindars as proprietary landholders.
context: The settlement formed part of late eighteenth-century Company state-building and was intended to stabilize revenue collection through a landed intermediary class. Its implementation varied across Bengal and affected cultivators as well as zamindars.
impact: Cornwallis's land policy reshaped agrarian power, landlord–cultivator relations, and colonial revenue administration in Bengal. Its long-term effects remain central to the history of rural property and indebtedness.
highlight: Governor-General associated with the 1793 Permanent Settlement in Bengal.
seoTitle: Charles Cornwallis and Bengal's Permanent Settlement
seoDescription: Learn how Charles Cornwallis's administration established the 1793 Permanent Settlement and reshaped land revenue in Bengal.
shortAnswer: Charles Cornwallis was the Governor-General whose administration implemented Bengal's 1793 Permanent Settlement.

faq.question: What was Charles Cornwallis's role in Bengal?
faq.answer: As Governor-General, he oversaw the administration that established the 1793 Permanent Settlement and reorganized Company governance.
